title: From 2 µm bins to physical cells
note: Open with the question of which physical cell produced each spatial barcode. This is a project progress report, not a claim of final validation.
source: Project H&E imagery; UIUC Vet Med wide-blue template.

title: Spatial RNA keeps expression in tissue context
lead: Bulk mixes cells; dissociated scRNA separates them; spatial methods map expression in tissue.
note: The published figure is cropped to its measurement-level row; the explanatory text below is ours. Bulk RNA-seq gives one mixed expression profile without resolving its cells or their positions. Dissociated single-cell RNA-seq gives a profile for each captured cell, but the original position of that cell in the tissue is lost. Spatial transcriptomics preserves a location for each measurement; its unit and resolution depend on the assay. Visium HD is the specific spatial assay on the next slide: it measures RNA in 2 µm squares, and those squares are not yet physical cells. Figure: Jeon et al., Biomolecules 2023, Figure 1, https://doi.org/10.3390/biom13020221, CC BY 4.0.
source: Jeon et al., Biomolecules 2023, Fig. 1 (top row cropped; CC BY 4.0).

title: Visium HD measures RNA in 2 µm squares
lead: Each square has a location and a gene-count vector.
note: Advance three times: first mark one orange barcode on the real H&E field, then zoom to the measurement square, then show its illustrative gene-count vector. The orange barcode and gene bars are illustrative, not measurements from the displayed tissue. Compared with standard Visium, the grid is much finer; unlike dissociated scRNA, tissue position remains available. A spatial barcode still does not identify its physical cell.
source: 10x Genomics Visium HD documentation; project H&E with illustrative grid and gene bars.

title: Cell-level questions need cell-level data
lead: Assigning RNA to the wrong cell can distort its profile and the interactions we infer.
note: Scientific significance: physical RNA ownership determines the profile assigned to each cell and its spatial neighbors. Potential impact, if reconstruction is reliable: stronger cell annotation and cell–cell communication hypotheses. Those downstream gains have not been directly validated in this progress report. Reconstruction keeps the original spatial information rather than discarding the bins.
source: Conceptual biological motivation; no quantitative claim.

title: A 2 µm bin is not a cell
lead: One cell spans many bins; a boundary bin may contain RNA from neighbors.
note: Do not equate the measurement unit with the biological unit. Each bin can be sparse for an individual gene and may cross a cell boundary.
source: Schematic; not an observed cell segmentation.

title: Bigger bins still do not show cell boundaries
lead: The same tissue and cell outlines look different under 2, 8, and 16 µm grids.
note: The three panels use one matched project H&E crop with simulated cyan cell outlines. Only the square grid changes. A larger square gathers more counts but can cross more than one cell; this does not mean native 2 µm bins are all empty.
source: 10x Genomics bin sizes; matched project H&E and generated-mask ROI; grid overlay schematic.

title: Boundary RNA can belong to either neighboring cell
lead: Two clear nuclei do not tell us which cell supplied RNA to a shared edge bin.
note: Hold on the orange boundary barcode. Image geometry gives two plausible nuclei, but it does not directly label the RNA's cell of origin. The next slide shows how existing tools infer the missing ownership.
source: Schematic boundary example; not an observed cell membrane.

title: Existing tools still infer where boundary RNA belongs
lead: Nuclear expansion and expression-guided assignment help, but the RNA source is not directly observed.
note: Bin2Cell grows supplied nuclear labels using image-informed expansion and an optional gene-expression supplement. STCS weighs distance and nucleus-derived expression. A distance-only control asks what spatial proximity alone can explain. These approaches are useful baselines; their limitations are assumptions about expansion, nuclear profile representativeness, or missing expression evidence, not a claim that every method fails everywhere. None directly observes the true source of each HD bin's RNA. In the selected saved Bin2Cell benchmark, GEX StarDist found zero secondary objects, so its observed output was mainly fixed expansion from external nuclei. Sources: https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btae546 ; https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.02.26.708370 .
source: Polanski et al., Bioinformatics 2024, btae546; STCS, bioRxiv 2026, 708370; project control.

title: Which physical cell supplied this bin's RNA?
lead: The central question is which physical cell produced the RNA at each barcode.
note: This is the single research question. First let the audience identify the orange boundary square and two plausible nuclei. The next slide states precisely what the method receives and returns. A boundary bin may have several biological RNA contributors; the output is a practical discrete owner for cell reconstruction, while the internal EM retains uncertainty.
source: HD-Cell-RL project objective; schematic.

title: H&E and RNA counts become cell assignments
lead: Inputs are H&E, physical nuclei, 2 µm gene counts, and an annotated scRNA reference.
note: Say the input and output in ordinary language. Inputs: aligned H&E image with confident nuclei, gene counts for physical 2 µm barcodes, and annotated scRNA reference expression. EM returns probabilities for candidate physical cells; the final method returns one owner per barcode and cell-level profiles. GT masks are for evaluation only.
source: HD-Cell-RL input schema and inference workflow; schematic.

title: Nuclei anchor cells before we assign and refine bins
lead: EM estimates a probability for each nearby cell; RL may revise uncertain hard assignments.
note: This is the contribution at the highest level, before detailed methods. Nuclear bins are protected anchors. Generalized EM considers every eligible nucleus in range and estimates soft ownership. Entropy identifies uncertain bins. The existing patch RL can replace only eligible hard owners under the global objective; this is the method architecture, not a claim that the current PPO has validated benefit.
source: HD-Cell-RL generalized EM and patch REPLACE architecture; schematic.

title: A simulated tissue gives us an answer key
lead: We build cells on a real H&E field, make bin counts, then hide the source labels during inference.
note: This is a map of the next part of the talk. The four matched panels show the same conceptual tissue field moving from nuclei to type labels to expanded regions and RNA compartments. The overview image is illustrative, not a measured whole-cell segmentation. The generator's source labels become an evaluation-only answer key.
source: Project simulation overview schematic: web/progress-report/assets/simulation-overview.jpg.

title: Simulation tells us where each bin's RNA came from
key: where each bin's RNA came from
lead: The generator records cell origin; inference sees only the resulting bin counts.
note: This is why pseudo data is useful. Synthetic truth is controlled but not automatically realistic.
source: Colorectal pseudo-HD generator; schematic.

title: We first find nuclei in the H&E image
lead: Real nuclear contours become the protected anchors.
note: The close-up shows saved StarDist nuclear contours on a real H&E field. The same crop appears on the cell-boundary expansion slide so the audience can compare the anchors with the later simulated masks. This step uses actual image structure rather than inventing nucleus positions.
source: Project nuclear segmentation ROI: web/progress-report/assets/nuclear_segmentation_cell_roi.png.

title: 8 µm RNA helps us label each nucleus
lead: Map each nucleus to its 8 µm parent bin, then compare the complete type probabilities.
note: The posterior values are the saved observed example for nucleus 80,653, not a threshold. Each nuclear 2 µm center inherits the parent 8 µm posterior. If one nucleus spans several parents, average the full vectors first and then take the maximum. The 8 µm grid and nucleus drawing are schematic.
source: Saved STHD nucleus 80,653 example in prior progress report; project annotation workflow.

title: Cell type and neighbors guide cell size
lead: A lymphocyte and a fibroblast should not grow to the same target area.
note: Target area comes from the nucleus-to-cell area prior and is constrained by nearby nuclei and geometry. The prior is a simulation assumption, not a universal constant.
source: Project pseudo-cell growth logic; schematic.

title: We simulate cell boundaries around each nucleus
lead: The matched H&E crop reveals how far the generated cell masks expand.
note: First show the real H&E crop with nuclear contours, then advance once to overlay the generated cell boundaries on exactly the same crop. Cyan outlines are generated masks, not measured cell membranes.
source: Project saved nuclear and expanded-cell ROI images.

title: One bin can contain RNA from more than one cell
lead: Exclusive image pixels can still give a 2 µm barcode fractional source ownership.
note: This is the geometry of fractional synthetic ground truth. The 65/35 values illustrate a possible crossing bin; they are not a measured fraction for this image.
source: Project fractional-bin GT logic; illustrative fractions.

title: Real scRNA cells supply the RNA profiles
lead: Generator cells and the EM reference come from independent donor sets.
note: The current generator draws from real annotated single-cell profiles rather than using scDesign3 to make every cell. Generator and reference donors are separated; type coverage gaps are reported rather than borrowing cells silently.
source: Colorectal real-scRNA pseudo-HD manifests and independent reference build.

title: We place RNA differently across three cell regions
lead: Nuclear, cytoplasmic, and membrane-associated molecules use different spatial patterns.
note: The distributions are schematic. Nuclear molecules are center-biased, cytoplasmic molecules spread through the interior, and membrane-associated molecules favor the edge. These are generator choices, not direct observations of each molecule's compartment.
source: Project compartment-placement logic; schematic kernels.

title: We count the simulated molecules in 2 µm bins
lead: Every placed molecule adds one count to its barcode and gene; its source is recorded separately.
note: Walk through the highlighted barcode: molecular dots land on a 2 µm grid, and counts are summed by barcode and gene. Known modeled-cell origins create the answer key. Unmodeled biological expression outside masks and technical background are distinct sources, not interchangeable ambient noise.
source: Colorectal pseudo-HD generator and realism audit; schematic counts.

title: We test the method on three kinds of data
lead: Each track answers a different validation question.
note: Track 1 has controlled but simulated ownership. Track 2 preserves Xenium molecule positions but is not measured Visium HD. Track 3 uses measured HD and Xenium on matched tissue, with alignment and cross-platform limits.
source: Project benchmark manifests; STCS-style Xenium notebook protocol; 10x paired lung data.

title: Every nearby nucleus can compete for a bin
lead: The candidate set includes every core or margin nucleus within the existing 20 µm limit.
note: Show the orange bin first. Advance to reveal all nuclei within MaxDis and the excluded fifth nucleus, then reveal one illustrative soft distribution. There is no nearest-three rule. The radius is environment.max_center_distance_um=20.0 from configs/episode_build.template.yaml, not the reward distance normalization. A nuclear seed stays locked to its owner.
source: HD-Cell-RL candidate MaxDis configuration; probabilities shown later are illustrative.

title: EM weighs every candidate before updating a cell
lead: All bins use the same cell beliefs in the E-step; the M-step then uses all updated soft owners.
note: Show current cell beliefs and locked nuclear seeds. Advance to the batch E-step, then the batch M-step, then the repeat loop. Given the current cell-type beliefs, the E-step scores all valid candidate cells for every bin at once, including margin cells. A single bin might be 0.52 for A and 0.40 for B. Nuclear seeds remain exactly one-hot. The M-step then uses the entire new responsibility matrix to update cell-type posteriors. In the current κ=2, γ=0 benchmark the physical nuclear expression profile is frozen while q updates; do not imply that component changes.
source: hd_cell_rl/em_assignment.py; illustrative probabilities.

title: Entropy shows which EM assignments are uncertain
lead: Uncertainty is normalized for the number of candidate cells.
note: The two illustrative bins each have four candidate cells. The clear distribution (0.95, 0.03, 0.01, 0.01) has normalized entropy 0.177; the uncertain distribution (0.52, 0.40, 0.05, 0.03) has normalized entropy 0.694. The first keeps EM owner A; the second may be inspected by RL. Normalization by log(candidate count) allows comparison across bins with different candidate counts. Ambiguity is gated only by normalized entropy, not top-one probability or top-two margin. A one-candidate bin has entropy zero.
source: HD-Cell-RL EM ambiguity rule; probabilities illustrative.

title: RL can change uncertain bin owners while nuclear seeds stay fixed
lead: EM gives a discrete starting owner; RL can test REPLACE for a high-entropy bin.
note: First show the EM-owned bin with two fixed nuclei. Advance once to show the discrete A → B REPLACE while the barcode and nuclei stay in place. This is the proposed integration path. The current PPO experiment is historical overfit; no fresh PPO training is claimed here. High-confidence EM bins are fixed by default in this experiment, while ambiguous bins may be replaced.
source: HD-Cell-RL patch environment and EM integration; schematic.

title: RL scores each change using the whole patch
lead: A REPLACE action earns the change in the global objective, not an EM probability bonus.
note: Expression includes the project's W1 and W5 concepts; geometry includes distance; local consistency includes neighborhood and overlap; shape compares plausible cell morphology. The score is objective after minus objective before. No EM-probability reward is added in version one.
source: hd_cell_rl/reward.py and patch global-delta environment; conceptual grouping.

title: PPO training has used only four patches
lead: This is an overfit integration test, not held-out validation.
note: The preserved PPO run was an overfit integration experiment on four patches. It should not be presented as held-out biological validation. Prior training and evolution artifacts remain untouched.
source: Preserved four-patch PPO training configuration and run.

title: We compare methods under the same rules
lead: The same nuclear seeds and scored core cells are used within each benchmark.
note: Bin2Cell expands supplied nuclei; STCS uses distance and nucleus-derived expression; distance-only EM removes the expression term; current EM adds reference-aware expression. Methods keep frozen native settings, so their radii are not forced to match. No SMURF or new PPO result is included.
source: Project five-method benchmark protocols; see linked run reports.

title: Adding expression does not always help EM
lead: In two Xenium-derived four-patch checks, fixed-setting EM trails its distance-only control.
note: These are four-patch mean full-grid per-cell IoU values. CRC: distance 0.7433 and current EM 0.4888. Lung 5K: distance 0.4363 and current EM 0.3799. They are diagnostic, not final held-out model selection. Candidate and GT coverage limitations remain, and the lung 5K data use native Xenium segmentation rather than manually drawn boundaries.
source: runs/benchmarks/xenium_notebook_crc_4patch_final_v2_20260924/report.md; xenium_notebook_lung_prime_5k_4patch_20260925/report.md.

title: Each benchmark has its own blind spots
lead: No one dataset is a complete stand-in for real cell ownership in Visium HD.
note: Pseudo data has known truth but can be too regular. Re-binned Xenium keeps observed transcript positions yet is not HD capture. Matched real HD/Xenium has genuine HD expression, but segmentation and registration are proxies for truth. Use all three in parallel.
source: Project pseudo-data realism audit and paired/Xenium-derived benchmark reports.

title: We need stronger validation before training PPO again
lead: First improve the data model, then freeze methods on fresh regions, then ask whether RL adds net value.
note: The near-term goal is not simply to make every method score lower. Match measurable real-HD properties, use independent regions or sections for comparison, and require a positive validation gain before another formal PPO run.
source: Project current evaluation plan.
